asof: Settles Fri 13 Nov 2026 · written Sat 14 Nov
headline: Soft PPI trims the front, the back keeps selling: Z6 and H7 1bp lower, Z9 up 6bp; U7 at 4.835% still prices almost four hikes.
summary: SR3 split around the peak after a slightly soft October PPI: Z6 and H7 fell 1bp in rate to 4.305% and 4.605%, M7 rose 0.5bp to 4.78% and U7 2bp to 4.835%, while Z7 through Z9 rose 2.5–6bp with Z9 leading at 4.64%. The week closed with U7 44bp, M7 41.5bp and H7 33.5bp higher in rate against 16bp in Z6; from the 30 October settle Z7 is up 32bp, U7 31.5bp and Z9 24.5bp. U7 is still the peak at 4.835%, 93.5bp over the 3.90% SOFR fixing, with only 19.5bp of easing priced from there to Z9, down from 23.5bp on Thursday. That is close to four hikes, against three in Bank of America's new call (December, January, March) and Deutsche Bank's, and two in Goldman's.
drivers: PPI cools the 50bp talk at the front

October PPI rose 0.3% against 0.4% expected with core in line at 0.3%, though the annual rate hit 6.5%, the highest since November 2022, and the PCE-linked components were softer. Two-year yields slipped 1.2bp to 4.872%, Z6 and H7 fell 1bp, and FedWatch eased to 27.1bp for December and 62.3bp by March from 28.3bp and 65.1bp.
Back end sells off again: a bear steepener past the peak

Ten-year yields rose 2bp to 5.153% and 30-year 2.3bp to 5.481%, and SR3 followed: U7 rose 2bp, Z8 4bp and Z9 6bp, so the inversion beyond the peak shrank even on a soft print. Brent held near $95.84 after Trump said no Iran deal is needed and tanker attacks in Hormuz continued, keeping inflation risk priced in 2028–29.

New York Fed President Williams, the FOMC vice chair, said inflation is persistent and policy still has work to do, after Logan called for at least two more hikes and Waller's 0.3% core-CPI bar for 50bp was met. Two-year notes were on track for their worst week since 2024, and H7–U7 ended the week 33.5–44bp higher in rate.

SOFR fixed at 3.90% on 12 November against EFFR at 3.88%, and reverse repo usage was just $0.325bn on Friday. U6, now driven by fixings, edged up 0.5bp to 3.93% ahead of Monday's refunding settlement.
spreads: The front of the curve stopped steepening and the inverted tail flattened. U6/Z6 fell 1.5bp to +37.5bp, Z6/H7 held at +30bp (+17.5bp week-to-date, +9bp on the month) and H7/M7 rose 1.5bp to +17.5bp (+8bp on the week, +5bp on the month), with M7/U7 up 1.5bp to +5.5bp; U7/Z7 rose 0.5bp to −2bp, so U7 stays the peak by 2bp over Z7 and 5.5bp over M7. Z6/Z7 widened 3.5bp to +51bp (+27bp week-to-date, +16bp on the month) and Z6/M7 1.5bp to +47.5bp (+25.5bp on the week, +14bp on the month). Past the peak every consecutive spread rose 0–0.5bp as the back led the selloff: Z7/Z8 is −12.5bp (+1.5bp on the day, −9bp on the week, −5bp on the month), Z8/Z9 −5bp (+2bp on the day) and U7/Z8 −14.5bp (+2bp on the day, −10bp on the week, −4.5bp on the month), with the 2029 spreads between −2bp and −0.5bp. The H7/M7/U7 fly was unchanged at +12bp (+3.5bp on the month) and M7/U7/Z7 rose 1bp to +7.5bp (+1bp on the month).
fed: The latest weekday fed funds futures snapshot, Thursday's, prices 28.2bp for 9 December (87% for 25bp, 13% for 50bp), 46bp by January, 63.7bp by March, 83.2bp by June and an 89.5bp peak by September 2027 (implied EFFR 4.775%). That compares with 28.9bp, 44.5bp, 62.2bp, 77.1bp and an 81bp peak on Wednesday, 16.2bp, 20.5bp, 30.5bp, 40.4bp and 43.5bp a week earlier on 5 November, and 17.6bp, 24bp, 37.3bp, 52.1bp and 57bp at the 30 October month-end: December is up 10.6bp on the month and the peak 32.5bp. Friday's FedWatch reading of 27.1bp for December and 62.3bp by March shows ZQ gave back a little after PPI, as SR3 did at the front. Adding SOFR's 2bp premium to EFFR, Thursday's ZQ path implies about 4.28% for Z6's December–March window and 4.79% at the September 2027 peak, so Z6 at 4.305% and U7 at 4.835% sit roughly 3bp and 4bp above it. Bank of America and Deutsche Bank expect three hikes and Goldman two, while Williams gave no endpoint; at nearly four hikes, the strip is still above the hawkish end of the forecasts.

ideas.title: Hold the short Z6/M7: the 2027 hike path is still overpriced
ideas.trade: Sell SR3Z6, buy SR3M7 (sell the Z6/M7 spread)
ideas.why: Open at +47.5bp, 0.5bp against us: soft PPI took 1bp off Z6's rate while M7's rose 0.5bp, and the spread is up 25.5bp week-to-date. It still prices almost two hikes after the first quarter, more than Bank of America's three-hike path that ends in March, and Williams set no endpoint. That is 8.5bp to target against 4.5bp to the stop.
ideas.risk: Strong October retail sales or hawkish FOMC minutes could add more mid-2027 hikes and push the spread above +52bp.

ideas.title: Keep the U7/Z8 flattener, with the stop close
ideas.why: Still open at −14.5bp, 3bp against us and 0.5bp from the stop: Friday's selloff was led by the back, with Z8 up 4bp in rate against 2bp in U7. We keep the stop where it is rather than widen it; the trade still offsets the core if hot data piles hikes into U7, and 19.5bp of easing remains priced from U7 to Z9. That is 8.5bp to target against 0.5bp to the stop.
ideas.risk: More oil- or term-premium-driven selling in the 2028 contracts would push the spread above −14bp and close the trade.

ideas.title: Stay neutral the front contract through refunding settlement

levels.Why neutral: fixings, not the Fed, drive it now

ideas.why: U6 edged up 0.5bp to 3.93% and is up only 1bp week-to-date, while H7–U7 rose 33.5–44bp. SOFR fixed at 3.90% on 12 November with EFFR at 3.88%, and only U6's last week sees the 9 December decision, so even a 13% chance of 50bp is worth little. Refunding notes settle on 16 November with reverse repo usage near zero, so there is little cash buffer.
ideas.risk: If settlement tightens funding, SOFR could print near 3.95% and cost a couple of bp.
